clue.text: Equipment for checking aircraft on carriers

definitions.text: Equipment for checking aircraft on carriers

blocks.clueFragment: Equipment for checking aircraft on carriers
blocks.note: surface reading: kit for inspecting planes aboard ships, as an engineer might
setter's reading: checking means halting, the cables that stop a landing jet on a deck

explanation.surface: Maintenance crews inspect warplanes on a naval flight deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checking' suggests inspection; here it means stopping, as in checking someone's progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrester gear is the set of deck cables that catch a landing plane's hook and bring it to a halt.

clue.text: Girl to catch in a bet

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, placed within its letters

blocks.note: to net something is to catch it
an ante is a stake placed before a hand of poker

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to win a girlfriend through a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Annette is a female given name, so it stands for any girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: When students may collect on the streets

definitions.text: When students may collect on the streets

blocks.clueFragment: When students may collect on the streets
blocks.note: surface reading: young people gathering outdoors, perhaps in a protest
setter's reading: collect means gather money for charity with tins

explanation.surface: Students crowd together in town, perhaps for a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag is the British name for students' annual charity fundraising, with stunts and street collections.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag days are the occasions when university students raise money for good causes in public.

clue.text: Desire transport?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about wanting to travel, or rapture of longing
setter's reading: Desire is the New Orleans tram line in Tennessee Williams's play title

explanation.surface: A passionate yearning, or simply wanting a ride somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is A Streetcar Named Desire, so the vehicle bearing that name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Tennessee Williams drama the tram whose destination sign read Desire is the vehicle in the title.

clue.text: They're used for cutting borders

blocks.note: first meaning: the sharp sides of blades
second meaning: margins or rims of something

explanation.surface: Garden tools trim the flower beds along a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests trimming a garden border; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades cut with their sharpened sides, and the outer limits of an area are likewise called that.

clue.text: It's high in theatrical circles

blocks.note: surface reading: something fashionable or esteemed in the acting world
setter's reading: circles are the tiers of seating in a playhouse, and this one is the top

explanation.surface: Something rates highly among actors and luvvies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatrical circles' sounds like the social world of the stage; dress circle and upper circle are literal seating levels.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost seating level of a theatre, above the circles, is the cheapest and highest balcony.

clue.text: Fast scoring rate

blocks.note: first meaning: a brisk musical tempo marking
second meaning: a speed written on a musical score

explanation.surface: A batsman piles on runs quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring rate' sounds like cricket or football; here the score is sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian tempo marking meaning lively and quick, written by composers on printed music.

clue.text: The aim of equal education?

blocks.note: surface reading: a policy goal of fair schooling for all
setter's reading: making things level, as a verb, and lessons held after dark

explanation.surface: A political aspiration for fair schooling across society.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'even' a class is to make it equal, and the answer is also adult tuition held at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult tuition held at night is called that, and the phrase also puns on levelling social ranks.

clue.text: In grave trouble, certainly in a pickle

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder and upheaval, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in serious difficulty is said to be in a pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pickle' means in a fix; read literally, it is where this sour liquid is always found.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickles are preserved by steeping in this acidic liquid, so it is literally always present there.

clue.text: Girl I sign on as an astronomer

blocks.note: informal word for a girl
taken as written
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A young woman joins up to study the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign on' looks like enlisting; 'on' just places the sign after the girl and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian scientist who turned a telescope on Jupiter's moons was a famous stargazer.

clue.text: Bound to fight in brave company

blocks.note: first meaning: set on combat, hostile and aggressive
second meaning: marching with Native American warriors, who are called braves

explanation.surface: Courageous soldiers are destined for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective; a brave is a Native American warrior, and their route to war gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means angry and ready for conflict, from the trail taken by warriors heading to raid.

clue.text: He's mad when the head takes action

definitions.note: the clue describes the person; the answer names him

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
a legal action is a case in court

explanation.surface: A headmaster loses his temper and sues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' suggests a headteacher, but it is slang for the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is informally called this, a slang noun for someone who is insane.

clue.text: Cunning oriental with slender frame

indicators.note: with, together with frame, says one piece is held by the surrounding one

blocks.note: E for east, the oriental direction
slight means slender; frame says it wraps around the other piece

explanation.surface: A wily man from the East has a thin build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' here means body build in the surface but signals an enclosing word in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means dexterous trickery or craftiness, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: The fewer you have the less you want

definitions.text: The fewer you have the less you want

blocks.clueFragment: The fewer you have the less you want
blocks.note: surface reading: a paradox about contentment with little
setter's reading: want means lack, so having fewer requirements leaves less lacking

explanation.surface: A proverb-like paradox about owning little and desiring little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as desire, but in its older sense means lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements or necessities; with fewer of them a person goes short of less.

clue.text: Snug place for young foxes?

blocks.note: surface reading: a den for fox cubs
setter's reading: cubs, whose burrow is a small cosy nook

explanation.surface: A cosy den where baby foxes curl up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as cubby plus hole it is a home for cubs; whole, it is a small cramped space.
explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosed nook or cosy compartment is called this, punning on a burrow for cubs.

clue.text: Where house-hunters may be found?

blocks.note: surface reading: an estate agent's office full of property seekers
setter's reading: players hoping to call house, the shout for a full card

explanation.surface: People looking for a home crowd an estate agency.
explanation.walkthrough: In British bingo, calling 'House!' claims a full card, so its players hunt for a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where people play the numbers game, marking cards until someone completes one.

clue.text: Score from an offside ball? Get away!

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, a cut is a stroke to the off side, then a run is scored
second meaning: flee quickly

explanation.surface: A footballer offside scores, and the protest is disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offside' points to football, but in cricket the off side is one half of the field, where a cut shot goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to escape hurriedly, abandoning things, and is also literally a cricket stroke followed by a run.

clue.text: It gets down to sorting the list

indicators.note: sorting means rearranging into a new order, so the letters are shuffled about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finally settles down to tidy a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets down to' sounds like starting work; the plant grows fluffy seed down.
explanation.definitionFit: This prickly plant produces feathery seed fluff known as thistledown.

clue.text: A river once more rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
again means once more

explanation.surface: A river's level goes up and down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rises and falls' reads as tidal movement; 'falls' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border are known by this name.

clue.text: Incorrect teaspoon set out in Indian city

indicators.note: out tells us the letters of the word set are taken away and left behind
incorrect means the remaining letters are not in their right order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A wrongly placed spoon at a table setting in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, E and T from teaspoon and rearrange what is left. Poona is the older spelling of Pune.
explanation.definitionFit: Pune, formerly spelt Poona, is a large city in Maharashtra state in western India.

clue.text: Report rewritten about one entertainer

indicators.note: something rewritten is put into a fresh order
about means around, so one part goes round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A journalist revises a story about a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a clown or stage performer in a white costume, from French pantomime.

clue.text: There's a number to be surrounded by gold in autumn

definitions.note: the month sits in autumn; the phrase describes it

indicators.note: surrounded by says the earlier pieces sit inside the later word, which encloses them

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golden autumn scene where some figure is ringed with gold leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the year falls in the northern hemisphere's autumn season.

clue.text: Manila's wild fauna

indicators.note: wild means unruly and out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: The wildlife of the Philippine capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the collective term for the creatures living in a region, as opposed to its plants.

clue.text: Brush and clean thoroughly

blocks.note: first meaning: low scrubby vegetation, brushwood
second meaning: to rub hard to clean

explanation.surface: Instructions for giving something a good wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' looks like a cleaning verb, but it is the noun for undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stunted bushes covering land and vigorous rubbing to remove dirt.

clue.text: The easiest dance to learn?

blocks.note: surface reading: which ballroom routine is simplest for a beginner
setter's reading: a dance with a single movement would need almost no learning

explanation.surface: A beginner wonders which ballroom dance to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: The one-step is a real early-twentieth-century ballroom dance; its name suggests only a single move.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragtime-era ballroom dance whose name implies just a solitary movement to master.

clue.text: Weather forecast favourable ? fear it's incorrect

indicators.note: incorrect means wrongly arranged, so the letters must be put into their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a sunny weather prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair is the barometer reading and forecasting phrase for settled, fine conditions.

clue.text: Little man devoured by a lion, perhaps a circus performer

indicators.note: something devoured ends up inside the eater, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: Rob is a shortened form of Robert
taken as written
a lion is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: A small man is eaten by a lion, perhaps at a circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little man' is a short name for a man, here Rob for Robert.
explanation.definitionFit: Big-top gymnasts and tumblers who perform feats of balance are called by this word.

clue.text: Travel agency for the young

blocks.note: surface reading: a firm booking holidays for young people
setter's reading: agency means means of conveyance, the thing that wheels a baby about

explanation.surface: A tour company specialising in student or youth trips.
explanation.walkthrough: The full formal word for a pram; 'agency' means the means by which babies travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby carriage pushed by hand, the full formal name behind the shortened word pram.
